cues: Sixteen lines in four quatrains, each built from two rhyming couplets: a a b b, c c d d, and so on.
All eight rhymes are perfect, and a couplet is the most settled rhyme in English: the ear gets what it is waiting for at once.
So in a poem about uncertainty and death, the sound keeps promising what the sense cannot.
The metre is mostly iambic tetrameter, the beat of hymns and ballads.
